bull.argument: The filing shows a business with strong current scale and profitability. Total 2025 revenue was $200.97 billion, up 22% year over year, and income from operations rose 20% to $83.28 billion. Growth was driven by both volume and price: ad impressions increased 12% and average price per ad increased 9%. Family daily active people reached 3.58 billion on average for December 2025, up 7%. Management is also investing heavily in future growth, citing AI initiatives that have already produced improved user engagement and monetization, and it reports $81.59 billion in cash and marketable securities against $58.74 billion of long-term debt. The bull case acknowledges real headwinds: the filing states that privacy regulation and iOS changes have reduced ad targeting effectiveness, Reels monetizes at a lower rate, and Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion in 2025. Even so, the financial results show that the core advertising engine is compounding faster than costs, which supports the investment case.

claims.claim: Revenue grew 22% in 2025 to $200.97 billion, with advertising as the driver.
claims.quote: Total revenue for 2025 was $200.97 billion, an increase of 22% compared to 2024, due to an increase in advertising revenue.

claims.claim: Growth came from both more ad impressions and higher pricing per ad.
claims.quote: Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps in 2025 increased 12% year-over-year, and our average price per ad increased 9% year-over-year.

claims.claim: Management reports AI investments are already improving engagement and monetization.
claims.quote: which we have already seen results in improved user engagement and monetization of our products.

bear.argument: The bull case leans on headline growth, but the filing shows that growth rests on fragile foundations. Substantially all revenue comes from advertising on Facebook and Instagram, and marketers carry no long-term commitments, so spending can fall quickly. The filing states that privacy regulation and Apple's iOS changes have reduced ad targeting and measurement, and that these effects will continue for the foreseeable future. Revenue growth of 22% was supported by a 9% rise in price per ad, and users are a concern: the filing notes that competitors such as TikTok have reduced engagement and that the Russia restrictions contributed to declines in the active user base. Reels monetizes at a lower rate than Feed and Stories. Costs are rising faster than the filing's framing suggests: costs and expenses grew 24% against 22% revenue growth, capital expenditures reached $72.22 billion, and Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion with similar losses expected in 2026. Operating margin fell from 42% to 41%. Long-term debt is $58.74 billion, and the effective tax rate rose to 30%.

claims.claim: Marketers have no long-term advertising commitments, so ad spend can shift quickly.
claims.quote: our marketers do not have long-term advertising commitments with us

claims.claim: Management expects privacy and platform changes to keep hurting ad revenue well into the future.
claims.quote: we expect that the legislative, regulatory and platform developments described above will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future

claims.claim: Reality Labs losses are large and expected to persist, and the company depends on other profits to fund them.
claims.quote: we expect our 2026 RL operating losses to remain similar to 2025

bull.argument: The bear case identifies real risks, and the filing states them directly: Reels monetizes below Feed and Stories, privacy and iOS changes constrain targeting, and Reality Labs will again lose about as much in 2026. But the reported results still show a business converting growth into profit. Revenue rose 22% to $200.97 billion, and operating income rose 20% to $83.28 billion. Costs grew faster than revenue, 24% against 22%, and operating margin slipped one point to 41%, so the bear's cost point is accurate, but the margin remains high. Pricing was not the only driver: impressions rose 12%, so both volume and price expanded. Family daily active people reached 3.58 billion, up 7%. The balance sheet held $81.59 billion in cash and securities against $58.74 billion of long-term debt. The 30% tax rate includes a one-time valuation allowance charge, and the filing says that without it the rate would have been 13%. The investment case depends on whether AI-driven engagement keeps outpacing costs and regulatory drag.

claims.claim: Operating income grew 20% to $83.28 billion, showing growth converted into profit despite higher costs.
claims.quote: Income from operations for 2025 was $83.28 billion, an increase of $13.90 billion, or 20%, compared to 2024

claims.claim: Ad impressions grew 12%, so growth was not driven by pricing alone.
claims.quote: Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps in 2025 increased 12% year-over-year

claims.claim: The 30% effective tax rate is inflated by a one-time valuation allowance charge; the underlying rate would have been 13%.
claims.quote: Absent the valuation allowance charge as of the enactment date, our 2025 effective tax rate would have decreased by 17 percentage points to 13%.

bear.argument: The bull case is right that a 41% operating margin and $83.28 billion of operating income are real, and the balance sheet is not the concern. The concern is whether the returns on spending hold. Costs rose 24% against 22% revenue growth, and margin fell a point. Capital expenditures reached $72.22 billion, and management says its AI initiatives will require significantly increased infrastructure investment, so cost pressure is likely to persist. Reality Labs lost $19.19 billion and is expected to lose a similar amount in 2026, and management says funding it depends on profits from other areas. The tax point cuts both ways. The 30% rate included a valuation allowance charge, and the filing says the rate would have been 13% without it, but that charge is still a 2025 cost. Growth also leans on pricing, with average price per ad up 9%, while Reels monetizes at a lower rate than Feed and Stories. Marketers have no long-term commitments, so that pricing and spend can change quickly.

claims.claim: Reality Labs losses are expected to persist, and funding them depends on profits from other businesses.

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes from the filing, with the bull's strongest points on revenue, operating income, and the valuation-allowance tax adjustment, and the bear's on marketer commitments, RL dependence, and AI infrastructure spend. In round 2 the bull directly addresses the bear's cost and margin points and the tax framing, while the bear reframes around return on spending and cost pressure, so neither side decisively wins the exchange.
